import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the relevant columns
columns_of_interest = [
    'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)',
    'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)',
    'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)',
    'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'
]

# Filter the dataset to include only the relevant columns
df_filtered = df[columns_of_interest + ['Country Group', 'Country Code']]

# Check for missing values
missing_values = df_filtered.isnull().sum()
missing_values

# Drop rows with missing values
df_filtered = df_filtered.dropna()

# Compute the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = df_filtered.corr()

# Display the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix

    'Labor force participation rate': 'SL.TLF.TOTL.ZS',
    'School enrollment, primary': 'SE.PRM.ENRR',
    'School enrollment, secondary': 'SE.SEC.ENRR',
    'Exports of goods and services': 'TX.VAL.TOTL.GD.ZS'
}

# Extract the relevant data

df_pivot = df_filtered.pivot(index='Country Code', columns='Series Code', values=[col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('19') or col.startswith('20')])

# Rename the columns for clarity
df_pivot.columns = df_pivot.columns.droplevel(0)
df_pivot.reset_index(inplace=True)

# Display the first few rows of the filtered and pivoted data
df_pivot.head()
